run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Every compose (create-post) request through nginx-thrift fails with HTTP 500 because compose-post-service cannot resolve the name 'user-service': it logs repeated 'TSocket::open() getaddrinfo() <Host: user-service Port: 9090> Name or service not known' / 'Failed to connect user-service-client' from 01:02:10 to 01:02:14 UTC. The user-service workload itself is healthy (Service, Endpoints and pod IP all match; pod Running/Ready with 0 restarts), and no NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace. The cause of the resolution failure is visible in the kube-system ConfigMap 'coredns': its Corefile carries an injected template block that answers NXDOMAIN for exactly 'user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local', and that ConfigMap was updated by kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-24T01:01:56Z, one second before the CoreDNS pod logged loading the new configuration. Affected: nginx-thrift (its own 500/error spans and logs on /wrk2-api/post/compose) and compose-post-service (its own DNS-failure error logs). Checked and healthy: user-service, and the other compose dependencies that were actually reached in the sampled trace.

claims.text: The ConfigMap kube-system/coredns Corefile contains an injected template plugin block: 'template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { match "^user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local\\.$" rcode NXDOMAIN fallthrough }', which answers NXDOMAIN for that single service FQDN; its metadata.managedFieldsSummary shows a kubectl-client-side-apply Update at 2026-11-24T01:01:56Z.

CoreDNS pod coredns-5f8886b457-wss8t (0 restarts) logged '[INFO] plugin/reload: Running configuration SHA512 = 0f2c93518620f96b239a636219cc11ef0cd81567bbdf51128c9ec637ff9e6b273ad0f5f43384d4556abac6d580ffb5ce8afa548dccd6de05ebd5ae1307321a82' at 2026-11-24T01:01:57Z, one second after the kube-system/coredns ConfigMap update, so the new Corefile (with the NXDOMAIN template) is the configuration in effect.

compose-post-service pod compose-post-service-659bfc5898-djmx7 (node sregym-worker2) logged, repeatedly between 01:02:10Z and 01:02:14.914Z, 'Thrift: Tue Nov 24 ... TSocket::open() getaddrinfo() <Host: user-service Port: 9090>Name or service not known' together with '<error>: (ClientPool.h:114:Pop) Failed to connect user-service-client'.

A cluster-wide Loki search over 2026-11-23T00:32:15Z-2026-11-24T01:02:15Z for 'Name or service not known|no such host|Temporary failure in name resolution|SERVFAIL' returned matching lines from only one app, compose-post-service, and every returned line was for 'Host: user-service'; the per-app 20-minute count shows compose-post-service with 75 such lines in the final minute and no other social-network application.

nginx-thrift serves the failing operation: its own spans for operation '/wrk2-api/post/compose' carry error=true, http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR (two spans at 01:02:10.935Z and 01:02:10.935Z), and its own log lines read '[error] ... [lua] compose.lua:62: ComposePost(): compost_post failure: Could not resolve host for client socket.'

In the complete failed trace 002042e623e1478d, compose-post-service's 'compose_creator_client' span (2148 us, no error status) has no corresponding server span in user-service, while its 'compose_unique_id_client', 'compose_text_client' and 'compose_media_client' spans do have matching 'compose_unique_id_server' (unique-id-service), 'compose_text_server' (text-service, which itself called url-shorten-service and user-mention-service) and 'compose_media_server' (media-service) spans - i.e. every other dependency name resolved and served, only the user-service call was never reached.

user-service is not the failing element: Service user-service exists with ClusterIP 10.96.150.8, port 9090->9090 and selector service=user-service (created 2026-11-24T01:01:40Z); its Endpoints contain 10.244.125.29:9090, which is the podIP of the Running/Ready pod user-service-7b68c97449-htz9l on node sregym-worker3 (restartCount 0).

All 27 pods in namespace social-network, including compose-post-service-659bfc5898-djmx7 and user-service-7b68c97449-htz9l, were Running, Ready and had restartCount 0 at query time; pods started 2026-11-24T01:01:41Z-01:01:45Z, and both CoreDNS pods (coredns-5f8886b457-nldb7 on sregym-worker, coredns-5f8886b457-wss8t on sregym-worker3) were Running/Ready with 0 restarts.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace social-network (query of kind networkpolicies returned zero objects), and no 'Connection refused'/'Connection refused'-style connect failures appear in the namespace's logs in the sampled window - the failures are name-resolution failures, not blocked or refused connections.

Incident timeline from the evidence: social-network Services and Deployments were created 2026-11-24T01:01:40-41Z by helm, compose-post-service logged 'Starting the compose-post-service server ...' at 01:01:45Z, kube-system/coredns was rewritten by kubectl-client-side-apply at 01:01:56Z, CoreDNS logged the new configuration SHA512 at 01:01:57Z, the wrk2 load generator started 'round #1' at 01:02:08Z, and the compose-post-service/user-service resolution errors and nginx 500s begin at 01:02:10Z.

The NXDOMAIN template rule held in ConfigMap kube-system/coredns for the name user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local is the root cause: it is the only DNS configuration targeting the exact host that compose-post-service's Thrift client fails to resolve, and the client-side error text (Host: user-service, 'Name or service not known') matches an authoritative NXDOMAIN for that name; the resulting compose_post_server failure propagates to nginx-thrift as HTTP 500 on /wrk2-api/post/compose.

user-service itself was checked and shows no failure of its own: the Deployment has 1 ready/1 available replica, the pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no previous terminated container, Endpoints resolve to that pod's IP, and it logged no errors after startup - so the compose failures are not caused by a dead, unready or mis-selected user-service.

Rejected: a namespace NetworkPolicy or a blocked/refused connection to user-service. No NetworkPolicy objects exist in social-network, and the observed error is getaddrinfo/EAI_NONAME name resolution, not a refused or timed-out TCP connect.

Rejected: cluster-wide or pod-wide DNS outage on compose-post-service. From the same pod, compose-post-service's calls to unique-id-service, text-service and media-service reached those services' server spans with no error in trace 002042e623e1478d, and no other social-network application logged a name-resolution failure in the window; only the name user-service failed.

The user-service startup log 'Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired ... user-mongodb:27017' at 01:01:43Z is most likely a startup-ordering transient of user-mongodb (user-service retried, then logged 'Starting the user-service server ...' at 01:01:44Z); no evidence ties it to the compose failures, which are pure name-resolution failures occurring before any connect.

Remove the 'template ANY ANY user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local { ... rcode NXDOMAIN ... }' block from the kube-system/coredns ConfigMap Corefile (keeping the kubeadm-managed kubernetes/forward/cache/loop/reload plugins), let the reload plugin pick it up, then verify from the compose-post-service pod that user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local resolves to 10.96.150.8 and that /wrk2-api/post/compose stops returning 500.

gaps: CoreDNS has no query logging enabled, so the NXDOMAIN responses themselves were not directly observed; the link between the Corefile template rule and the client error is the exact-name match plus the reload timing (ConfigMap write 01:01:56Z, CoreDNS config load 01:01:57Z, first errors 01:02:10Z).
The authorized window ends at 2026-11-24T01:02:15Z, so whether the NXDOMAIN rule was later reverted and whether compose 500s stopped afterwards is unknown.

Cluster-scoped Calico resources (globalnetworkpolicies.crd.projectcalico.org, networksets.crd.projectcalico.org) exist as CRDs but are not readable with the available tools; only namespaced networkpolicies were checked (zero objects).
Whether user-service's mongodb index creation succeeded on its retry is unknown (no further user-service log lines, and user-service received no traffic in the sampled traces).

The wrk2 load generator's summary captured in the window ended at 01:02:07Z, before the failures began; its error/latency totals for the failing round are unknown, so end-user error percentage is not quantified.

Traces are a biased sample from an in-memory Jaeger started with the environment, so the absence of user-service server spans is only shown for the specific trace fetched (002042e623e1478d), not for all requests.
next_steps: Revert the injected template block in ConfigMap kube-system/coredns and confirm CoreDNS reloads and answers A 10.96.150.8 for user-service.social-network.svc.cluster.local.
After the fix, re-check compose-post-service logs for 'Failed to connect user-service-client' and nginx-thrift for HTTP 500 on /wrk2-api/post/compose to confirm recovery.
Audit who/what applied the kubectl-client-side-apply change to the kube-system/coredns ConfigMap at 2026-11-24T01:01:56Z (change-history integration is not available in this run).
Verify user-service can reach user-mongodb:27017 and created its indexes, since its startup log recorded a server-selection timeout at 01:01:43Z.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
